title: feat(plugin-list,app-shell): a console list's toolbar grouping lives in the URL (objectui#11860)
body:
Fixes #11860

Clause-②: yes — `@object-ui/plugin-list`'s published `ListViewProps` gains one optional member, `onGroupingChange`; nothing else on any published surface moves, and a host that does not pass it behaves as before.

Grouping is the last of the card's four pieces. The other three (the Filter panel's conditions, the search term and the sort) landed in objectui#11915; this PR follows the same pattern. With it, all four pieces of the maintainer's contract are delivered: 「视图、筛选、排序、分组都写进 URL；临时界面（面板、弹窗）不写进 URL。」

## What changes

**`ListView` (`@object-ui/plugin-list`) reports a user's grouping change.**
- New optional prop `onGroupingChange(grouping)`, beside `onSortChange` and `onFilterChange`. The value is the spec's `GroupingConfig` (`@objectstack/spec/ui`), or `undefined` when the grouping is cleared.
- Every user door goes through one callback, `changeGrouping`:
  - the toolbar Group panel's editor (a level added, changed or removed);
  - its Clear button;
  - the setter handed to the compact View settings popover, which covers that popover's editor and its Clear.
- The schema re-sync effect still calls the state setter directly, so a changed `schema.grouping` is not echoed back. That is the same rule `onSortChange` follows for a view's declared sort.

**The console object page (`@object-ui/app-shell`) writes it to `uf__group` and opens a list grouped by it.**
- `userFilterUrlState.ts` gains `LIST_GROUP_PARAM` (`uf__group`). The value is the `GroupingConfig` serialized as JSON. The key is reserved, so `parseUserFilterParams` never hands it to `UserFilters` as a quick-filter field. This also applies to `InterfaceListPage` and `ObjectDataPage`, which call that parser.
- The read has the same shape as the sort read:
  - level by level through `GroupingConfigSchema.shape.fields.element`, then the envelope through `GroupingConfigSchema` itself;
  - a value that is not JSON, a level or envelope the spec refuses, or a level naming a field the object does not declare or the user cannot read is dropped. The field gate is the one objectui#11915 put on the other pieces, including `perms.checkField` once permissions have loaded;
  - nothing throws, and the list still opens.
- `ObjectView.tsx` uses the existing seed machinery (`listSeedRef` / `ownListParamsRef` / `writeListUrlState`) without forking it:
  - the seed carries `grouping`;
  - the relay passes `grouping: listSeed?.grouping ?? listSchema.grouping` into `schema.grouping`, which `ListView` already reads;
  - `onGroupingChange` writes `uf__group` with replace;
  - the grouping is written to the URL only, not to the view and not to the per-browser cache.

## Measured against the dispatch's mechanism assumptions (on `989b1908`)

- **H1, one door: holds after this change.** On the base, `groupingConfig` is set in four places: the toolbar editor's `onChange`, its Clear button, the setter handed to `ViewSettingsPopover` (whose editor and Section Clear both call it), and the schema re-sync effect. The three user call sites now fire the callback, and the re-sync does not. Pinned by `ListView.onGroupingChange-11860.test.tsx`: the toolbar editor (add, flip order, remove), toolbar Clear, popover add and popover Clear all fire. A host-side `schema.grouping` change is re-read, the editor shows `Descending`, and `onGroupingChange` is not called.
- **H2, the spec shape is the URL shape: holds.** `GroupingConfigSchema.parse` returns the editor's own `GroupingConfigValue` unchanged. This is measured in the unit test, and in a pre-edit probe of the spec on its own. One bound was found, see Acceptance notes: the schema refuses `{ fields: [] }` (`too_small`), so a cleared grouping has no URL form.
- **H3, precedence: holds, pinned both ways plus the control.**
  - A link's `uf__group` wins over the view's declared grouping.
  - Without one, the declared grouping stands, and the address bar carries none.
  - A change is written with `REPLACE` only, and Back leaves the list in one step.
  - A view switch opens the next view on its own grouping, and Back restores the link's.
  - Opening and closing the Group panel leaves the query string and the navigation count unchanged.
- **H4, other hosts unchanged: holds.** The only non-test site that passes `onGroupingChange` is `ObjectView.tsx`. The 124-file app-shell union, which includes every `InterfaceListPage` and `ObjectDataPage` importer, passes unchanged.

## Also in this PR: a sort-precedence fix in the same file (bounded in-place fix)

**Measured with a throwaway probe, now deleted.** On a view that declares `sort: [name asc]`, a link carrying `uf__sort=[due_date desc]` produced a query with `$orderby` = `name asc`, while the address bar still showed `due_date desc`. The control, the same link on a view with no declared sort, queried `due_date desc`.

**Cause.** `renderListView` wrote `sort` twice. The first write is the rung objectui#11915 taught to put the URL's sort first. The second is a later `...(viewDef.sort?.length ? { sort: viewDef.sort } : {})` spread, left over from before that rung existed, which overrode the rung on every view that declares a sort. The spread is removed. It was redundant with the rung in every other case: for an empty `viewDef.sort` the rung already yields it.

**Why it is fixed here.** All four in-place conditions hold:
- it is the same class as this card: URL-carried list state must win over the view's declared value;
- it is a mechanical one-line removal, in the shape objectui#11915's own comment and changeset declare ("an opened link sorts as it was sorted");
- `ObjectView.tsx` is already in this claim's file surface, and no other open PR touches it;
- it needs the same test file and the same gates.

**Pin and changeset.** The fix is pinned by a new `describe` in `ObjectView.listUrlState-11860.test.tsx` that covers both directions, and it is named in the changeset.

  - `@object-ui/plugin-grid` is now imported, and `find` returns one row in the grouping block, so a grouped grid mounts and asks for its groups. The grouping is read off the `queryGroupHeaders` request, at the data source.
- `ObjectView.relayRungCensus-7559.test.ts`: the `grouping` absence reason now says the relay writes the key only to lay a URL grouping over it. It reads no `viewDef`, so the census still classes it as `relayed-upstream`.

## Acceptance notes

- **A cleared grouping has no URL form.** `GroupingConfigSchema` requires at least one level, so clearing deletes `uf__group`. On a view that declares a grouping, a link therefore cannot carry "no grouping": it opens on the declared one. This follows the ruling (read through `GroupingConfigSchema`, drop on invalid). It is not worked around with a sentinel of this module's own. The report raises it as an open question.
- **Files beyond the four named regions:**
  - one `import type { GroupingConfig }` line at the top of `ListView.tsx`;
  - the sort fix above, in `ObjectView.tsx`;
  - the census reason line;
  - the one-sentence edit to the pending `.changeset/11860-list-url-state.md`: "Toolbar grouping is not included yet." is deleted, because this PR makes it false and both entries would publish in the same release.
- **No README sentence was changed.** `packages/plugin-list/README.md` and its "With Callbacks" example are outside the claim's file surface. Offered to the seat: one line after "End users can also add or remove grouping fields at runtime via the Group toolbar button", saying that a host hears each change through `onGroupingChange`.
- **Observation, read in source only and not filed.** The compact View settings popover's hint reads "Grouping, color, density, and visible fields. Applies to everyone who uses this view." Toolbar grouping is not stored on the view: it was component state before this PR and lives in the URL after it.

## Out of scope, measured as the dispatch asked (not fixed)

**The quick-filter carry-over across a view switch reproduces.** It was measured with a throwaway probe, now deleted, in the same harness: this page, `plugin-view`'s `ObjectView` and `ListView` render for real, and `window.location` was set to the router's entry, because `initialUfSelections` reads it.
- **Steps:** open `view/qa?uf_priority=urgent`, then navigate the same mounted page to `view/qb` (no query string).
- **Result on `qb`:** the query still carried `["priority","=","urgent"]`, the chip read "Priority1", and the address bar's search was empty.
- **Control:** `view/qb` opened fresh queried with no filter.
- **Cause, as read:** `initialUfSelections` is captured once per mount. That path is not edited here. The finding is reported for the seat to file.
